candidate.blueprint_locator: 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan, Management of Care, printed p.7 / PDF p.11
candidate.educational_objective: Describe the safety-focused purpose of purposeful nursing rounds.

options.A: Proactively ask about needs such as toileting and pain and check the environment for safety concerns.
options.B: Avoid asking about needs so the client will use the call light when necessary.
options.C: Use rounding only after a client has already fallen.
options.D: Replace all unscheduled nursing assessments with a fixed rounding checklist.

candidate.rationale: AHRQ fall-prevention materials describe purposeful rounding as consistent bedside rounds that address personal needs and standard safety elements, including asking whether the client needs the bathroom and checking the environment. Rounding complements rather than replaces individualized assessment.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Purposeful rounding proactively addresses patient needs and incorporates standardized safety checks such as toileting and environmental assessment.
candidate.source_document_title: Preventing Falls in Hospitals—Purposeful Rounding materials
candidate.source_locator: Falls Prevention Toolkit webinar/slides—purposeful rounding; standardized elements include toileting and environmental checks
candidate.source_organization: Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality
candidate.stem: A nurse performs purposeful bedside rounds at regular intervals. Which action best reflects the purpose of this rounding?
